basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Defines the shape of what may leave a system: which elements, at what grain, with which treatments.
Holds no instance data; it operates on schemas and policies only.
Differs from the access contract (WM-XCT-002), which says who may read, and from runtime enforcement (WM-XCT-038).
References cohort floors and privacy budgets from their instruments instead of restating them.

may: Compile an output template from a shape and a source schema.
Preview a shape against a schema to show what would leave.
Derive the least-disclosure shape for a stated purpose.
Detect source schema drift that makes a template stale.
mustNot: Serve data from an uncompiled or stale template.
Let unnamed elements leave by default.
Restate or lower a cohort minimum or privacy budget locally.
Mark a shape as assured without a declared assurance method.
requiresHuman: Approving a new or widened disclosure shape.
Classifying a disclosure change as material.

considerations: Poorly designed shapes allow re-identification of people from aggregated or pseudonymised data.
Overly strict shapes can block legitimate research and public interest uses.
Small groups can be singled out; cohort floors protect minorities in data.

items: A shape names source schema elements, selection rules, grain, treatments and an assurance method.
Confused with an access grant, a database view, a privacy notice and a data contract.
Leakage of new fields after schema drift.
False assurance from an expired method.
ISO/IEC 20889 privacy enhancing data de-identification techniques.
